captions: Your voice is gone. You shouted every single minute.
Sunday league final. 4:40 p.m. You're on the bench.
2–1. Seventy-eighth minute. The whole bench is standing.
From the street behind the stand, faintly: Allahu akbar.
Old Yusuf, the kit man, spreads his jacket behind the bench.
He prays. You keep shouting. “After the whistle,” you tell yourself.
The whistle. Photos. The car. Maghrib is gone.
Next Sunday. Half-time. The cold tap in the changing room.
Water on your hands. A hoarse whisper: Bismillah.
This time you stand beside Yusuf. Four minutes. The match can wait.

post.caption:
90 minutes on your feet. Not 4 for Maghrib? ⚽

The adhan drifted over the stand in the 78th minute. Old Yusuf prayed behind the bench. You kept shouting — “after the whistle.”

“Establish prayer for My remembrance.” (20:14)

Maghrib is soon. Be on your feet for it.
